Container.Name: Bexton
Container.Overview:
The Sexton — chat memory, voice, ears and music for teamspeak.phatt.vip, in one container (PHA-3099 / PHA-3428).
Runs, under supervisord: the Sexton bot and its audio bridge (one tsclientlib connection, one bot account), a local whisper.cpp server with ggml-base.en baked in, the bgutil POT provider with pinned ffmpeg/yt-dlp for the music lane, and — option (a), Brandon 2026-09-12 — its OWN OpenClaw gateway running the teamspeak channel plugin.
Because the plugin runs in here, the bridge, whisper and the POT provider are reached over loopback and nothing has to be mounted into the main OpenClaw container. IMPORTANT: disable the teamspeak channel on the main gateway before starting this, or both gateways answer every message. There is no CLI for that — set channels.teamspeak.enabled to false in its openclaw.json and restart it. image/deploy.sh does this for you, after confirming this container has taken the channel over. See image/README.md in the repo.
Container.Requires: The `phattvip` Docker network, with teamspeak6-server on it.

Config.Name: Logs
Config.Description: The on-disk markdown chat log, one file per channel per day. Also what the bot rehydrates its history from on connect, so losing it loses the catch-up PM's memory.

Config.Name: Config
Config.Description: Two things live here. sexton-id.txt is the bot's TeamSpeak identity — it IS its server-side UID and permissions; lose it and the Sexton comes back as a stranger. openclaw/ is the in-container gateway's whole config and state tree, including the channel config and the plugin install record. Both are 0600 and both belong in your backups.

Config.Name: Channel
Config.Description: Channel name to sit in. Case-sensitive — it is resolved against the server's channel tree at startup.

Config.Name: TeamSpeak host
Config.Description: Container name of the TS6 server on this network. Leave as-is; the public hostname hairpins and gets flood-scored.

Config.Name: Identity file
Config.Description: Path, inside the container, to the identity string. Prefer this over passing the identity as a variable — a variable is visible in `docker inspect`.

Config.Name: Agent
Config.Description: The gateway agent this container's channel binds to. 'bexton' seeds the Bexton persona (AGENTS.md/SOUL.md/IDENTITY.md) into the gateway workspace on first boot and binds the channel to it.

Config.Name: Wake names
Config.Description: Comma-separated names that wake the bot in voice. Lower-case variants are added automatically.

Config.Name: House band
Config.Description: 1 = compose_song / band_status are on and the band leader announces and plays generated songs. Generation costs money on every provider that can do it.

Config.Name: Band generator
Config.Description: minimax (its endpoint refuses NEW accounts, status 2153 — works only for an existing paying music customer), suno-api (a self-hosted gcui-art/suno-api; set the URL below), or command (an executable under /config/band/ that writes the file; see the plugin README).

Config.Name: suno-api URL
Config.Description: Only for the suno-api generator: base URL of the self-hosted suno-api, e.g. http://suno-api:3000.

Config.Name: Band command
Config.Description: Only for the command generator: the executable, inside the container. /config is the Config path above, so /config/band/generate is /mnt/user/appdata/bexton/config/band/generate on the host.

Config.Name: Whisper threads
Config.Description: CPU threads for local transcription. 4 is the PHA-3228 setting; raise it only if the box is otherwise idle, since this competes with everything else on the RAID.

Config.Name: Duck gain
Config.Description: Music-lane gain floor (0..1) while someone is talking. Reaches the floor in 50ms, recovers in 800ms.

Config.Name: In-container gateway
Config.Description: 1 = this container runs its own OpenClaw gateway with the teamspeak plugin (option (a), the deployed design). 0 = don't; that is the rollback to option (b), and it also means you must re-enable the teamspeak channel on the main OpenClaw gateway and point its bridgeUrl at ws://sexton:9099.

Config.Name: Gateway port
Config.Description: Control port for the in-container gateway. Not published to the host by this template; it is here so it can be changed if it ever collides on a custom network.

Config.Name: Log level
Config.Description: Rust tracing filter for the bot and bridge.
